title: Unconditional NP-hardness at the Goemans–Williamson Max-Cut threshold
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: For every rational \(\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon <1- \alpha _{\mathrm{GW}}\), do rationals \(0<b<a\le 1\) with \(b/a<\alpha _{\mathrm{GW}}+\varepsilon\) exist such that distinguishing Max-Cut value at least a from value at most b is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions?
definitions: For a finite simple undirected graph with at least one edge, its Max-Cut value is the maximum fraction of edges crossing a bipartition. Let \(\alpha _{\mathrm{GW}}=\min _{0<\theta \le \pi} 2\theta /(\pi (1- \cos  \theta ))\). NP-hardness means there is a polynomial-time map from 3-CNF formulas to graphs mapping satisfiable formulas to the at-least-a case and unsatisfiable formulas to the at-most-b case. The reduction and constants may depend on \(\varepsilon\). No Unique Games or other hardness conjecture is assumed.

context_blocks.text: The Goemans–Williamson approximation ratio is a landmark in semidefinite optimization. Matching hardness from ordinary NP-hardness would identify that ratio as an intrinsic computational threshold under \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\).

Known optimal hardness follows from Unique Games; it is not an unconditional NP-hardness theorem. The target deliberately concerns the reduction itself, so a conditional implication from UGC does not count as a solution. This separates the problem from the Unique Games conjecture and from improving a particular rounding algorithm.

why: Determine whether a defining semidefinite approximation threshold follows from ordinary NP-hardness alone.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
